architecture.mechanism: Self-adaptive closed-loop control of lubrication flow and pressure using a BLDC-driven inner rotor pump with PID trapezoidal wave control, adjusting output in real time based on monitored pump speed, pressure sensor feedback, and vehicle speed.
architecture.intervention: Install a BLDC motor-driven inner rotor oil pump with an electronic pressure sensor and PID control module on the 2020 Honda Civic manual transmission, routing the pressure-plate engagement hydraulic actuator supply through this adaptive pump so that clutch-engagement line pressure is increased on demand during acceleration events (e.g., ~35 mph) to prevent engagement failure-induced surge.
architecture.expected_effect: Maintains consistent and adequate hydraulic pressure at the clutch pressure plate under varying driving conditions, eliminating the forward surge during acceleration by ensuring reliable, adaptive clutch engagement regardless of speed or load transients.
architecture.falsification_test: Bench-test the 2020 Honda Civic clutch actuation system on a dynamometer simulating the ~35 mph acceleration event, with and without the adaptive BLDC pump module, recording pressure-plate disengagement/engagement timing, actuator line pressure, and any resulting driveline torque spikes over 1000 repeated cycles; the mechanism is falsified if surge-equivalent torque transients still occur at pressures the adaptive pump is commanded to deliver.
